subject: Cox regression beta coefficient seems not converge

messages.author: 7794973310e701f9
messages.subject: Cox regression beta coefficient seems not converge
parts:
Dear Stan users,

I am modeling a PKPD time-to-event data in a hierarchical fashion. Specifically for each subject's data there are five variables: ID (Subject ID); TIME (follow-up time); event (event indicator);  DOSE (drug dose level); PK (PK exposure). I want to use summary PK data (by DOSE level), instead of individual subject data to construct the model. Suppose there are K dose levels. Briefly speaking, the hierarchical model is:

Linear model for "PK vs. DOSE": PK_mean_k = logphi_1 + logphi_2 * log(DOSE_k) + epsilon; (k = 1, ..., K)
Cox model for "TIME/EVENT vs. PK": lambda(t | PK_mean_k) = lambda_0(t) * exp(beta * PK_k).

I followed the counting process notation for cox model as showed in this Leuk example. In this example, "Y i (t) is an observed process taking the value 1 or 0 according to whether or not subject i is observed at time t ". Since I use summary data, the different in my case is that  I count "Y i (t)" as the number of at-risk subjects at time t for dose level k. (So N i (t) counts the number of failures which have occurred up to time t at dose level k in my case.)

As a result, the parameters for the linear model part converge very well. However, the four chains of beta coefficient for Cox model don't mix well (See attached pdf file) so I am concerned with the convergence of beta. There are NO warning/exception messages about divergence at all after Stan sampling though.

My questions are: (1) for the model part, am I doing the right thing or off the track? (2) is the convergence of beta coefficient a concern? How could I improve that? (3) the "pairs" plot shows there is a perfect correlation between "logphi_1" and "logphi_2" (intercept and slope), would that be a concern?

I attached my stan model file and a plot file. Thank you very much for any comments!

Yaohui
